questions.title: Excursion payments
questions.stimulus:
A school records excursion payments in a relational database. The contents of the Students and Payments tables are shown. Amount is in dollars.

**Students**

| StudentID | Name | Year |
|---|---|---|
| ST1 | Mia Wong | 11 |
| ST2 | Jack Hill | 12 |
| ST3 | Omar Haddad | 11 |
| ST4 | Ruby Nguyen | 11 |
| ST5 | Tom Reid | 12 |
| ST6 | Isla Park | 11 |

**Payments**

| PaymentID | StudentID | Amount | Paid |
|---|---|---|---|
| P1 | ST1 | 120 | No |
| P2 | ST2 | 150 | No |
| P3 | ST3 | 85 | Yes |
| P4 | ST4 | 95 | No |
| P5 | ST5 | 60 | No |
| P6 | ST6 | 140 | No |
| P7 | ST3 | 40 | No |

parts.prompt:
The school wants a list of the Year 11 students who have not yet paid for the excursion, showing each student's name and the amount owing, with the student who owes the most listed first.

Write an SQL query to produce this list.

marking_criteria.criterion: Provides a substantially correct SQL query with at least TWO of: joining the tables; both conditions (Year 11, not paid); ordering by amount descending
Shows some understanding of joining or filtering

parts.sample_answer:
```
SELECT Students.Name, Payments.Amount
FROM Students, Payments
WHERE Students.StudentID = Payments.StudentID
  AND Students.Year = 11
  AND Payments.Paid = 'No'
ORDER BY Payments.Amount DESC
```

Result:

| Name | Amount |
|---|---|
| Isla Park | 140 |
| Mia Wong | 120 |
| Ruby Nguyen | 95 |
| Omar Haddad | 40 |

Traps: 'owes the most listed first' is the ORDER BY (in the middle of the sentence, not at the end); Omar Haddad paid one payment but still owes $40; Jack Hill and Tom Reid are Year 12.

questions.title: Streaming report
questions.stimulus:
A streaming service records each time a user watches a show in the Views table. The contents of the Views table are shown.

**Views**

| ViewID | UserName | Show | Genre | MinutesWatched | Device |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V01 | kira | Bluey | Comedy | 30 | TV |
| V02 | sam | The Night Agent | Drama | 52 | TV |
| V03 | kira | Heartbreak High | Drama | 45 | Phone |
| V04 | li | Bluey | Comedy | 12 | TV |
| V05 | sam | Fisk | Comedy | 28 | Laptop |
| V06 | ava | Planet Earth | Documentary | 58 | TV |
| V07 | li | The Night Agent | Drama | 60 | TV |
| V08 | ava | Fisk | Comedy | 41 | TV |
| V09 | kira | Planet Earth | Documentary | 20 | TV |
| V10 | sam | Utopia | Comedy | 35 | Phone |

parts.prompt:
Construct a SQL query that displays, for each genre:

- the genre
- the number of views, with the heading Views
- the average minutes watched, with the heading AvgMinutes

Only include views of at least 30 minutes that were watched on a TV. List the results from the lowest to the highest average minutes watched.

question.dataset_setup_sql:
CREATE TABLE Views (ViewID TEXT PRIMARY KEY, UserName TEXT, Show TEXT, Genre TEXT, MinutesWatched INTEGER, Device TEXT);
INSERT INTO Views VALUES ('V01','kira','Bluey','Comedy',30,'TV'),('V02','sam','The Night Agent','Drama',52,'TV'),('V03','kira','Heartbreak High','Drama',45,'Phone'),('V04','li','Bluey','Comedy',12,'TV'),('V05','sam','Fisk','Comedy',28,'Laptop'),('V06','ava','Planet Earth','Documentary',58,'TV'),('V07','li','The Night Agent','Drama',60,'TV'),('V08','ava','Fisk','Comedy',41,'TV'),('V09','kira','Planet Earth','Documentary',20,'TV'),('V10','sam','Utopia','Comedy',35,'Phone');

marking_criteria.criterion: 1 mark each: COUNT and AVG with the AS headings; WHERE with both conditions (>= 30 AND Device = 'TV'); GROUP BY Genre; ORDER BY AvgMinutes ASC

parts.sample_answer:
```
SELECT Genre, COUNT(ViewID) AS Views, AVG(MinutesWatched) AS AvgMinutes
FROM Views
WHERE MinutesWatched >= 30 AND Device = 'TV'
GROUP BY Genre
ORDER BY AvgMinutes ASC
```

Result:

| Genre | Views | AvgMinutes |
|---|---|---|
| Comedy | 2 | 35.5 |
| Drama | 2 | 56.0 |
| Documentary | 1 | 58.0 |

Traps: 'at least 30' is >= (V01 is exactly 30); TV only; lowest to highest is ASC.

questions.title: Hawks goal table
questions.stimulus:
A local football league stores players and goals in a relational database. Each row in Goals is one goal. The contents of the Players and Goals tables are shown.

**Players**

| PlayerID | Name | Team |
|---|---|---|
| PL1 | Kai Lomu | Hawks |
| PL2 | Ben Doyle | Sharks |
| PL3 | Leo Grant | Hawks |
| PL4 | Max Ortiz | Hawks |
| PL5 | Sid Rana | Sharks |

**Goals**

| GoalID | PlayerID | Round |
|---|---|---|
| G01 | PL1 | 1 |
| G02 | PL2 | 1 |
| G03 | PL3 | 1 |
| G04 | PL1 | 2 |
| G05 | PL2 | 2 |
| G06 | PL2 | 2 |
| G07 | PL4 | 3 |
| G08 | PL1 | 3 |
| G09 | PL3 | 3 |
| G10 | PL5 | 3 |
| G11 | PL1 | 4 |

parts.prompt:
The coach of the Hawks wants the following report.

| Player | Goals |
|---|---|
| Kai Lomu | 4 |
| Leo Grant | 2 |
| Max Ortiz | 1 |

Write an SQL query that produces this result.

marking_criteria.criterion: Provides a substantially correct SQL query with at least TWO of: joining the tables; restricting to the Hawks; COUNT with GROUP BY; renaming and ordering
Shows some understanding of joining or grouping

parts.sample_answer:
```
SELECT Players.Name AS Player, COUNT(Goals.GoalID) AS Goals
FROM Players, Goals
WHERE Players.PlayerID = Goals.PlayerID
  AND Players.Team = 'Hawks'
GROUP BY Players.PlayerID
ORDER BY Goals DESC
```

Traps: only Hawks players appear (Ben Doyle has 3 goals but plays for the Sharks); Goals is a COUNT of rows (no number column to SUM); order by Goals DESC, not by name.

questions.title: Who watched what (reading)
questions.stimulus:
A streaming service records each time a user watches a show in the Views table. The contents of the Views table are shown.

**Views**

| ViewID | UserName | Show | Genre | MinutesWatched | Device |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| V01 | kira | Bluey | Comedy | 30 | TV |
| V02 | sam | The Night Agent | Drama | 52 | TV |
| V03 | kira | Heartbreak High | Drama | 45 | Phone |
| V04 | li | Bluey | Comedy | 12 | TV |
| V05 | sam | Fisk | Comedy | 28 | Laptop |
| V06 | ava | Planet Earth | Documentary | 58 | TV |
| V07 | li | The Night Agent | Drama | 60 | TV |
| V08 | ava | Fisk | Comedy | 41 | TV |
| V09 | kira | Planet Earth | Documentary | 20 | TV |
| V10 | sam | Utopia | Comedy | 35 | Phone |

parts.prompt:
The following SQL query is run on the Views table.

```
SELECT UserName, Show
FROM Views
WHERE Genre = 'Drama' OR Genre = 'Documentary' AND Device = 'TV'
ORDER BY MinutesWatched ASC
```

Type the table of results produced by the query, with its column headings.

marking_criteria.criterion: Provides the correct output, including the correct rows and ordering
Provides some correct rows OR correct rows in the wrong order

parts.sample_answer:
| UserName | Show |
|---|---|
| kira | Planet Earth |
| kira | Heartbreak High |
| sam | The Night Agent |
| ava | Planet Earth |
| li | The Night Agent |

Trap (harder than HSC): AND is worked out before OR, so this means Drama (on any device) OR (Documentary on a TV). kira's Heartbreak High on a Phone is included. Sorted by MinutesWatched even though that column is not displayed.

parts.prompt: Write an SQL query to display the shortest and the longest time spent watching a comedy, with the headings Shortest and Longest.

question.dataset_setup_sql:
CREATE TABLE Views (ViewID TEXT PRIMARY KEY, UserName TEXT, Show TEXT, Genre TEXT, MinutesWatched INTEGER, Device TEXT);
INSERT INTO Views VALUES ('V01','kira','Bluey','Comedy',30,'TV'),('V02','sam','The Night Agent','Drama',52,'TV'),('V03','kira','Heartbreak High','Drama',45,'Phone'),('V04','li','Bluey','Comedy',12,'TV'),('V05','sam','Fisk','Comedy',28,'Laptop'),('V06','ava','Planet Earth','Documentary',58,'TV'),('V07','li','The Night Agent','Drama',60,'TV'),('V08','ava','Fisk','Comedy',41,'TV'),('V09','kira','Planet Earth','Documentary',20,'TV'),('V10','sam','Utopia','Comedy',35,'Phone');

marking_criteria.criterion: Correctly uses MIN or MAX, OR correctly restricts to comedies

parts.sample_answer:
```
SELECT MIN(MinutesWatched) AS Shortest, MAX(MinutesWatched) AS Longest
FROM Views
WHERE Genre = 'Comedy'
```

Result:

| Shortest | Longest |
|---|---|
| 12 | 41 |

Trap: no GROUP BY needed; one row for the whole filtered table.
